A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RCaGP research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including the additional material and checklist in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original UCI regression results, Bayesian optimization experiments, and ablations in Table 1, Figures 3–4, and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, a DJIA flash-crash case study, and RBF-kernel regression results.

M1.justification: The RCaGP inference equations, robust weighting, ELBO/EULBO objectives, action optimization, and expert-guided mean procedure are retained. The new relevance-pursuit adaptation is a comparison baseline; suggested RKHS projections are not incorporated into the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Section 7.2 adds a focused financial time-series case study using DJIA observations during a flash crash, extending evaluation to naturally occurring market anomalies. The four UCI datasets, four BO tasks, and existing contamination scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds two substantive robustness comparators: SVGP with Student-t likelihood and SVGP adapted with relevance pursuit, labeled RRP. v1 evaluated only SVGP, CaGP, and RCSVGP against RCaGP. The BO and uniform/focused-outlier comparisons retain their original comparator sets.

E3.justification: Appendix A and new Table S3 introduce an additional RBF-kernel evaluation on clean and asymmetrically contaminated UCI data, supplementing the existing Matérn-5/2 setting. Retained experiments keep their reported metrics, contamination procedures, training settings, and BO initialization.

E4.justification: The RBF experiment tests sensitivity to kernel choice. The DJIA case study adds diagnostics comparing predictive means and robust weight functions under market anomalies. Existing threshold sensitivity, expert-mean ablations, and contamination analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new checklist explicitly states that the 20 BO repetitions use different seeds. v1 already reported 20 repetitions and standard-deviation bands, so this is additional seed disclosure, not evidence of more runs or a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained, but v2 adds substantial baseline and RBF results plus DJIA prediction curves. In Table 1, added RRP achieves Yacht MAE 0.356 versus RCaGP's unchanged 0.435. New Table S3 shows kernel-dependent exceptions: RCSVGP has lower contaminated-data MAE and NLL than RCaGP on Boston and Parkinsons.

T1.justification: New Appendix F.3 introduces Proposition F.4 and an ELBO/Schur-complement derivation for SVGP relevance pursuit, including a claimed optimal noise adjustment and leave-one-out formulas. Section 4 also states an additional RKHS norm condition. The original RCaGP propositions and appendix proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and concluding scientific claims retain the same scope: joint robustness and computation awareness, conservative uncertainty, an expert-guided mean, and superior regression/BO performance. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 4 substantially develops the applicability limits of the existing RKHS assumption: the nonlinear correction may fall outside common RBF/Matérn RKHSs, motivating projection or alternative kernels. It adds a residual-based misspecification interpretation. New experimental discussion addresses RRP's accuracy/runtime tradeoff and attributes DJIA behavior to joint robustness and computation awareness.

D1.justification: Section 7 adds an implementation repository link, and the checklist states that companion code and running instructions will be supplied. Existing hardware, runtime descriptions, hyperparameters, dataset access information, and expert-mean implementation details are retained; reordering Appendix I is not a technical change.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ament et al.'s relevance-pursuit work and positions its SVGP adaptation as a baseline. It removes Wilson et al.'s reparameterization-trick citation alongside the BO background paragraph. The related-work taxonomy and principal novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the narrative structure are retained. Local revisions remove the BO primer, expand the theoretical explanation, insert new subsections, rename Discussion to Conclusion, and reorder Appendix I. Affiliations, acknowledgments, and a NeurIPS checklist are also added or updated.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel DJIA Figure 3, expands Table 1 with two baselines, and adds RBF Table S3. Existing BO and ablation plots become Figures 4–5 without changed curves. Figures S1–S3 move to the appendix's end, while the overall visual format remains.

improvement.justification: The added robust baselines and RBF results expose performance limits absent from v1, while the RKHS qualification and code link improve transparency. These provide a limited overall gain. Counterbalancing weaknesses include performance summaries that overstate Tables 1/S3 and Proposition F.4's exact-optimizer claim despite a derivation that explicitly discards a term.
